summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Tail Latency Mitigation; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [low] For a real Google system with 10ms latency at the 99% percentile for any single request, the 99% percentile for all requests to finish is 140ms, and the 95% percentile is 70ms. Sources: https://blog.acolyer.org/2015/01/15/the-tail-at-scale/

[low] TTFT-calibrated hedging achieves comparable tail improvement at roughly 19.8 percent overhead and only fires on the slow twenty percent, the actual cache misses, leaving normal requests untouched. Sources: https://infoq.com/articles/adaptive-hedged-requests-p99-latency

[low] Static hedge thresholds appear effective in benchmarks but break in production as latency distributions shift with load, deployments, and time of day, requiring continuous manual tuning that rarely happens in practice. Sources: https://infoq.com/articles/adaptive-hedged-requests-p99-latency
